subject: English
passage: Many works of the Greek philosopher Theophrastus (4th-3rd century BCE), including his history of philosophy, On Monarchy, have been lost to time. Scholars wishing to read a work written by the Greek philosopher needn't ______ they can still obtain a copy of Theophrastus's Historia Plantarum, a treatise on botany.
prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: Choice D is the best answer. The convention being tested is punctuation use between independent clauses. The text contains two independent clauses: 'Scholars wishing to read a work written by the Greek philosopher needn't despair, though' and 'they can still obtain a copy of Theophrastus's Historia Plantarum.' In this choice, 'though' functions as a trailing concessive adverb modifying 'despair,' set off by a comma. The semicolon after 'though' correctly separates the two independent clauses.
